    > **Branch:** `provenance` (moved from `main` 2026-11-14)

    > **Completed:** 2026-11-15 git:913bf05

    - **Found (2026-11-11, on `vecclone`; also on its base's stdlib):** `impl<T: Clone> Clone for Vec<T>` and `impl<T: Clone> Clone for Option<T>` declare `#[borrows()]`, so a clone holds no borrow: `return v.clone();` of a local `Vec<[u8]>` holding a view of a stack array, and `return o.clone();` of `Some(s)`, are accepted and read the dead frame (gap_77, gap_78, recorded in git:e7b4d6c: `exit 7` where the frame held 42). Returning `v` itself is refused (`cannot return 'v' a reference into storage owned by this frame`), and so are `s.clone()` of a slice directly (`region escape`), `clone_in`, and a `#[derive(Clone)]` struct holding the view (`region escape: returning a pointer to local stack storage via sret`). The same attribute hid the store from `extend_from_slice`'s summary once it cloned each element (probe 418 accepted); id:z0173 declares `#[stores(slice -> self)]` there instead.
    - **Route class:** a generic `#[borrows()]` impl whose result is built from a `T` that may be a view. Probe every generic `#[borrows()]` function in `stdlib/` (`rg -B3 '#\[borrows\(\)\]' stdlib`), not only `Clone`.
    - **Promoted (2026-11-14, the maintainer's request):** from `future.tm.md`, with the five other open soundness holes on `main`, ahead of the provenance and ZIL series: each is a program `main` accepts and should refuse (or a drop it skips), one session-sized fix. Order among them: the reads of a dead frame first (id:z0183, id:z0180), then the `fn`-value faults (id:z0100, id:z0101), then the skipped drop (id:z0176) and the unchecked bound (id:z0175). Any "after the `vecclone` series merges" note above is met: the series is on `main`, with gap_76 to gap_79 in `bench/safety_matrix/probes/`.
    - **Also (2026-11-14, id:z0183):** a user `impl Clone for H` returning `H { s: self.s }` hides the view the same way, with no `#[borrows()]`: `out.resize(1, H { s: &buf })` and `extend_from_slice` of an array of such structs put a frame view into the caller's `Vec` (`gap_80`, git:891b76e, exit 77). The result of a function that loads a view through a reference parameter and returns it in a struct is not tied to the parameter (`reach`, not `storage`, in `verify.zrl`'s `storage_facts`). Flip `gap_80` with this task's fix, or say why it is a different route.
    - **Moved (2026-11-14, a reviewing session, by the maintainer's "use provenance as much as possible"):** under `--provenance` (`provenance` at git:a6bd53a), `gap_77` and `gap_78` are refused (`error: provenance: the returned value holds an address of this frame (return ...`), and so is `gap_80`'s route. This task becomes the provenance tests for them, as id:z0183's are: placed after the merge of `main` into `provenance` (id:0m61c), because the probes use `main`'s `impl Clone for Vec<T>` and `Option<T>` (the `vecclone` series), which that branch lacks.
    - **Settled (2026-11-15, on `provenance` `4deb429`):**
      - Under `--provenance`, `build/zoril` already refuses `bench/safety_matrix/probes/gap_77_vec_clone_launders_frame_views.zrl` (`error: provenance: the returned value holds an address of this frame (return rule)`), `bench/safety_matrix/probes/gap_78_option_clone_launders_frame_view.zrl` (`error: provenance: the returned value holds an address of this frame (return rule)`), and `bench/safety_matrix/probes/gap_80_struct_view_cloned_into_callers_vec.zrl` (`error: provenance: the callee stores an address of this frame into memory that outlives it (call store rule)`), while without `--provenance` all three compile (`exit 0`).
      - `tests/language/memory/provenance/struct_view_cloned_extend_refused.zrl` already covers `extend_from_slice` of `H { s: &buf }`; `gap_80` itself tests `out.resize(1, H { s: &buf })`.
      - Nuance on `Vec<u8>.clone()` (`stdlib/clone.zrl:14-28`): because `Vec.clone` calls `Vec::<T>.new_in_raw(self.raw_arena())`, its origin summary has `return O={ParamContents(0)} S={Param(0)}`, which ties the returned `Vec` in `O` to `S(v) = {Frame(_1)}` when `v` is a local `Vec::<u8>.new()` inside the callee (so returning `v.clone()` of a local `Vec<u8>` is also refused under `--provenance`, whereas `clone_param_vec(v: &Vec<u8>) -> Vec<u8> { return v.clone(); }` is accepted). `clone_opt() -> Option<i32>`, `clone_opt_view(s: [u8]) -> Option<[u8]>`, and `fill(out: &mut Vec<H>, b: [u8])` calling `out.resize(1 as usize, H { s: b })` compile cleanly under `--provenance` (`exit 0`).

      4. `tests/language/memory/provenance/clone_returned_accepted.zrl` (`// flags: --provenance`, `// expected exit 0`): `clone_param_vec(v: &Vec<u8>) -> Vec<u8> { return v.clone(); }`, `clone_opt() -> Option<i32> { let o = Option.Some(7); return o.clone(); }`, `clone_opt_view(s: [u8]) -> Option<[u8]> { let o = Option.Some(s); return o.clone(); }`, and `fill(out: &mut Vec<H>, b: [u8]) { out.resize(1 as usize, H { s: b }); }`, called from `main` and checking the returned values.

    - **Do (1) — `scripts/test_runner_output.sh` (`check_mode`, lines 52–67):** detect when `timeout` is already absent from `PATH` (`! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1`) and exclude `hangs.zrl` with `EXPECTED_TOTAL_NO_TIMEOUT` in `quiet`, `default`, and `verbose` modes just as `opts_hidden` does:

    ```sh
    check_mode() {
        mode="$1"
        out="$TR_WORK/output.$mode"
        expected="$EXPECTED_TOTAL"
        exclude=""
        if ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            expected="$EXPECTED_TOTAL_NO_TIMEOUT"
            exclude="tests/runner/fixtures/tests/hangs.zrl"
        fi
        mkdir -p "$TR_WORK"
        case "$mode" in
            quiet)   TR_EXCLUDE="$exclude" "$RUNNER_UNDER_TEST" --timeout 2 --quiet $FIXTURES > "$out" 2>&1 ;;
            default) TR_EXCLUDE="$exclude" "$RUNNER_UNDER_TEST" --timeout 2 $FIXTURES > "$out" 2>&1 ;;
            verbose) TR_EXCLUDE="$exclude" "$RUNNER_UNDER_TEST" --timeout 2 --verbose $FIXTURES > "$out" 2>&1 ;;
            opts_hidden)
                shim="$TR_WORK/shim_opts"
                path_without "$shim" git timeout setsid valgrind dprint rustc
                expected="$EXPECTED_TOTAL_NO_TIMEOUT"
                TR_EXCLUDE=tests/runner/fixtures/tests/hangs.zrl PATH="$shim" "$RUNNER_UNDER_TEST" --timeout 2 $FIXTURES > "$out" 2>&1
                ;;
        esac
    ```

    - **Do (2) — `scripts/check_user_tools.sh` Part 2 (lines 61–71):** capture `real_git="$(command -v git)"` before creating `$git_shim_dir/git`, and in `$git_shim_dir/git` after logging to `$USER_TOOLS_GIT_LOG`, delegate to `$real_git` when `$caller` matches `*scripts/version.sh*` (the only caller allowed by line 85's `grep -v 'scripts/version.sh' "$git_log"`), exiting `1` for all other callers:

    ```sh
    real_git="$(command -v git)"
    cat << EOF > "$git_shim_dir/git"
    #!/bin/sh
    caller=\$(ps -o args= -p "\$PPID" 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
    printf '%s: git %s\n' "\$caller" "\$*" >> "\$USER_TOOLS_GIT_LOG"
    case "\$caller" in
        *scripts/version.sh*) exec "$real_git" "\$@" ;;
    esac
    exit 1
    EOF
    chmod +x "$git_shim_dir/git"
    ```

The guard's assignment drops `e`'s old value with its payload, and `s` is dropped again at the end of the arm: the counter reads 2 where 1 is due (`bench/safety_matrix/probes/gap_84_match_guard_mutates_scrutinee.zrl`, `exit 7`). With a skipped `_` part (`P.A(s, _) if { e = P.B; true }`) the drop of the skipped part reads the overwritten payload and the program segfaults (exit 139). The compiler at git:c161107, before id:qm667, behaves the same: the hole is older than that batch.

    - **Route class:** a write to the scrutinee's place, or to a place it contains, inside a match guard after the arm's by-value bindings were made. Probe for the fix: a direct assignment, a field assignment (`w.a = ..` on a struct scrutinee), a `&mut self` method, `&mut e` passed to a function, an assignment in a nested block or closure in the guard, and `if let ... if` / `while let` if they take guards.

The alternative, binding by reference while the guard runs and moving after it passes (Rust's own lowering), still has to refuse the write for the `&` bindings, so it adds work without accepting more. - [x] +safety +borrowck +AI-D @main A binding made by matching through a `&mut` reference keeps its borrow of the referent (gap_85) id:37p40
    > **Created:** 2026-11-14
    > **Branch:** `main`
    > **Depends:** id:g63ny
    > **Placed:** after the check-in id:g63ny that found it, with the open soundness holes on `main` and before the stage1 backport id:jhy7v and the merge id:0m61c. It goes before id:a47b8 only so that a deep-thinking session can take it straight after the check-in; the two are independent.
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-14 git:1b1d147

    - **Found (2026-11-14, check-in id:g63ny, probe git:56ea75e):** `fn g(e: &mut Q, p2: *mut u8) { match e { Q.A(s) => { *e = Q.A(S { p: p2 }); bump(s); }, Q.B => {} } }` is accepted: the old payload is dropped and `bump(s)` reaches the new one (`bench/safety_matrix/probes/gap_85_binding_through_mut_ref_outlives_write.zrl`, `exit 77`). With `enum QB { A(Box<i32>), B }` and `*e = QB.B` (or `tb(e)`), `return **s;` reads freed memory and segfaults (exit 139, `build/vvtam/p/b_body.zrl`, `c_direct_write.zrl`). The same happens with `if let QB.A(s) = e` (`c_iflet.zrl`), with a local `let e = &mut q; match e { .. tb(e) .. }` (`c_local_refmut.zrl`), and with a match guard that calls `tb(e)` (`b_guard.zrl`). Not a route: `match &mut q { QB.A(s) => { q = QB.B; **s } }` is refused (`cannot assign to 'q' because it is borrowed`), and so is `let s = &h.b; th(h);` (`cannot mutably borrow 'h' while it is already borrowed`). `build/zoril-stage1` accepts `b_body.zrl` too, so the hole is long-standing.
    - **Lead:** a pattern that matches through a reference binds with `Let(s, Ref(place))` (`bind_pattern_name`, `src/lower_zir/lower_match.zrl`) where `place` is under `Deref` of the `&mut` local. The explicit `&h.b` path records a borrow that `check_zir`'s conflict check sees on a later `&mut *h`/write. Compare the region given to the binding's `Ref` and how `check_zir.zrl` treats a borrow whose place goes through `Deref` of a `&mut` local, against `&(*h).b`.
    - **Do:** diagnose the cause and fix it, or settle the fix in this text and re-tag `+AI-G` if it turns out mechanical. Flip gap_85 to `compile_reject`, probe the route class (match, `if let`, `while let`, a guard, a nested pattern `Q2.A(Q.A(s))`, a struct pattern, and a `&mut` field `h.q` as the scrutinee), and run the rejection differential: the fix makes the checker refuse more, so every newly refused program is listed with its reason.
    - **Checks:** C1 gap_85 `compile_reject` and `run_safety_matrix.sh` `Mismatches: 0`; C2 an error test with the routes above, one error per function in the direct compiler output; C3 an accepted test where the binding is dead before the write (`match e { Q.A(s) => { let n = bump(s); *e = Q.B; } }`) runs with the right drop count; C4 take the fix out and watch C2 compile and gap_85 run (`exit 77`); C5 `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`, its `fresh (no cache)` line quoted, every newly refused program listed; C6 `make test`, its `Total:` quoted.
    - **Cause (2026-11-14, a reviewing session):** a pattern that matches through a reference binds with `Let(s, Ref(*t..))`, where `t = EnumPayload(scrut)` is the payload's address (`lower_variant_match`, `src/lower_zir/lower_match.zrl`). `check_borrow_creation` (`src/check_zir.zrl`) recorded the borrow on `*t..`, rooted at `t`, which nothing writes. `EnumPayload` inherits only the borrows its source already holds, and a `&mut` parameter or local holds none, so a later `*e = ..` or `&mut *e` overlapped no live borrow. `match &mut q` was refused only because its scrutinee temporary holds a borrow of `q`. `check_zir` already kept `t → scrut` in `enum_aliases`, but used it only for moves.
    - **Fix:** in git:1b1d147 on `main`. `check_borrow_creation` also records the borrow on the enum the address came from: `enum_payload_borrow_root` follows `enum_aliases` from the leading `Deref` (nested payloads too) to `*src` for a reference source or `src` for a value, and `place_in_arena` copies the place. The extra borrow is the whole enum, since no projection names a variant's payload. It is made only for a named borrower: the first version, without that condition, refused `match_skipped_parts_dropped.zrl` (`cannot move out of borrow`, 22 errors), because `note_skipped`'s compiler-made address of a skipped part, which the arm drops after moving another part out, then borrowed the whole enum. A pattern binding is always named, and a copy of it (`let r = s`) inherits the borrow. `doc/spec/surface_syntax.md` (the paragraph "Tuple, struct and payload patterns see through a reference") now states the rule. The `Borrow Aliasing (Exclusive Mutable)` row in `safety_model.md` and `matrix.md` names the `&mut` case and cites gap_85; class (M) and the Known gaps entry are removed; and the counts and figures are updated (370 `compile_reject`, 46 `known_gap`, 18 holes; 47,777 compiler lines, 850 `unsafe { }` blocks, `4.68%`, `1,941 of 41,517`). The fuzz record (`bench/fuzz/README.md`) is stale for this change to `src/`.
    - **Routes probed** (`build/vvtam/p/`, `QB { A(Box<i32>), B }`), all refused now: `match e` with `tb(e)` or `*e = ..`, `if let`, `while let`, a guard, a nested pattern `Q2.A(QB.A(s))`, a local `let e = &mut q`, a struct pattern `match h { HB { b: s, .. } => { th(h); **s } }`, and a `&mut` field `match r.q` with `tb(r.q)`. Still accepted, with the right result (exit 42): the binding read before the write (`match`, `if let`, nested), a field read through `r.q`, two bindings `QP.A(a, b)`, a write through the binding (`**s = 41`), and a shared `&QB` parameter.

    > **Created:** 2026-11-11

    - **Found (2026-11-09, git:6ad43a6, while working on id:z0162):** `match e { E.A(s) => { let n = 1; }, E.B => {}, }` moves the payload into `s`, and neither `s` nor `e` is dropped: the destructor never runs. A leak on its own, but it breaks "drop exactly once" (`doc/spec/safety_model.md`), and a guard that is never released (a lock, an fd, an `Arena` reset) can be a correctness hole. Reproducer (`S` counts its drops into `*p`; exits 0, should exit 1):

    ```zoril
    struct S { p: *mut u8 }
    impl Drop for S { fn drop(self: &mut S) { unsafe { *self.p = *self.p + 1 as u8; } } }
    enum E { A(S), B }
    fn main() -> i32 {
        let mut flag = 0 as u8;
        let fp = &mut flag as *mut u8;
        {
            let e = E.A(S { p: fp });
            match e { E.A(s) => { let n = 1; }, E.B => {}, }
        }
        return flag as i32;
    }
    ```

    - **Do, first:** probe the siblings on the current tree and count the drops each makes (0, 1 or 2): the payload used (`consume(s)`, one drop in `consume`), a `_` arm, a nested pattern, `if let`, a struct payload, a tuple payload. Record each count here; a 0 is a `known_gap` probe (with the Known gaps entry and a `doc/SAFETY.md` §6 class), a 2 a `known_gap` probe that also stops this task for the maintainer before the fix. Then fix in the same session only if it is one mechanism; otherwise split.
    - **Checks:** C1 each sibling's drop count quoted; C2 the probes recorded and `sh scripts/run_safety_matrix.sh` `Mismatches: 0`; C3 `make test`, its `Total:` quoted.

Order among them: the reads of a dead frame first (id:z0183, id:z0180), then the `fn`-value faults (id:z0100, id:z0101), then the skipped drop (id:z0176) and the unchecked bound (id:z0175). Any "after the `vecclone` series merges" note above is met: the series is on `main`, with gap_76 to gap_79 in `bench/safety_matrix/probes/`.

    ```zoril
    struct S { p: *mut u8 }
    impl Drop for S { fn drop(self: S) { unsafe { *self.p = *self.p + 1 as u8; } } }
    enum E { A(S), B }
    fn take(e: E) -> S {
        return match e { E.A(s) => s, E.B => { return S { p: 0 as *mut u8 }; }, };
    }
    fn main() -> i32 {
        let mut n = 0 as u8;
        let np = &mut n as *mut u8;
        { let s = take(E.A(S { p: np })); }
        return n as i32;
    }
    ```

Only the method-call receiver is missed.

Measured with `gdb` (`catch syscall close`, printing the result) while compiling a three-line program importing `core.zrl` and `vec.zrl`: generation 1 makes 29 closes that succeed and 9 that return `-9` (`EBADF`); `build/zoril` makes 29 and none. Harmless today only because nothing is opened between the two closes; one `open` between them would close an unrelated descriptor. The 277 `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`/`.ok()`/`.err()` calls in `src/` take route 2 too, on types with no destructor.

    ```zoril

    if !(scrut_tag == ILTYPE_PTR || scrut_tag == ILTYPE_PTRMUT || scrut_tag == ILTYPE_BOXED || scrut_tag == ILTYPE_BOXEDMUT) {

    }
    ```

- [x] +testinfra +decision +AI-D @testinfra id:z0113 T9 One verification record for the author and the reviewer: a result cache keyed by inputs
    > **Created:** 2026-11-06
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Asked by:** the maintainer.
    > **Before:** id:z0112 (the review rule it changes), id:z0114.
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-14

    - **The stamp's record (the maintainer, 2026-11-07):** a cache keyed by inputs decides what not to run, as the unchanged-tree stamp did. The stamp needed four fixes (id:z0142, id:z0143, id:z0144, id:z0150) and was removed (id:z0154), because a defect in it reports a pass for code that was not tested. Before recommending a cache, say what in its design keeps it from failing the same ways (a key that misses an input, a record taken at the wrong moment, a lookup that depends on git), and how a reviewer sees a wrong hit.

    - **Now:** the check-in rule ("the model that wrote a fix does not close it") has the reviewer rerun everything itself, rightly: it does not take the author's word. So every safety task pays for `make test` and `make preflight-changed` twice on the same tree: about 4 min for each `make test`, and 13 to 15 min for each preflight with the differential. Having the author skip the suites would hand over unverified work, and a failed review costs more than a run.
    - **Idea:** a result is a function of its inputs, not of who ran it. Key each item (per-file test, probe, gate, scenario, differential program) by a hash of everything it reads: the test file and its imports, `build/zoril`, `build/zilc`, `build/zbuild`, the runtime objects, the toolchain fingerprint (`scripts/test_qbe_fingerprint.sh`'s), its flags, and the runner and gate scripts. Store the verdict and a digest of its output under `build/cache/`. Each side builds the compiler from the commit itself, so the reviewer computes every key independently. A key that matches means the same inputs, and the reviewer takes only the verdict from the cache.
    - **What keeps the reviewer honest:** in review mode (`REVIEW=1` or `make review`) the cache serves hits, but these items rerun in full: a random sample (10%, with its seed printed), every item whose inputs the change touched, every failure and skip, and the task's reproducers and sibling probes. A sampled item that disagrees with its cached verdict invalidates the whole cache, forces a full run, and is a finding: a nondeterministic test or a stale key.
    - **Decide:** the key's inputs for each item kind, and how an undeclared input is caught. A gate reads files a test file does not, so gates may need a list of their inputs, or stay uncached. Also decide where the cache lives, so a reviewer in another worktree or a cloud session can use it (a directory under `build/`, or an exported tarball of keys and verdicts), and how the completion note cites a run (tree hash, cache key set, sample seed).
    - **Measure first:** is `build/zoril` byte-identical when built from the same commit in two checkouts (the stage1 path and the `build/zoril` path)? Is the test output deterministic across runs? The static-image and repro gates already check part of this. If the builds are not identical, the key uses the compiler's source hash and the test proves that the source hash determines the binary. Then implementation tasks: the per-file cache, the reviewer sampling, the gate cache.
    - **Measure first, answered (id:z0123, 2026-11-13, at git:58983a0):** yes, the builds are identical. `zoril`, `zilc` and `zbuild` are byte-identical across two checkouts at different paths, across the stage1 path and two self-rebuilds, and against the main tree's incremental build. Verdicts are deterministic: two `make test` runs gave identical `--results` (1,203 items, all `PASS`) and the same `Total:` counts. Output is deterministic except for elapsed seconds in two scenario lines, pids in two shell messages that tests provoke on purpose, and one corpus program that prints memory past its string (id:1kaye). Details, commands and what was not measured are in id:z0123.
    - **Order (id:z0103, 2026-11-06):** after the tiers (id:z0115) and the differential's caches (id:z0114), which take most of the saving with fewer inputs to declare. Its implementation goes in the runner, if id:z0117 decides on one. Its keys and verdicts are kept as plain files under `build/` (the series rule), so a `sh` script and a Zoril runner can read the same cache.
    - **Review (2026-11-06):** the header's **Before:** id:z0112, id:z0114 is stale: by the bullet above and id:z0112's own order bullet, this task follows id:z0114 and id:z0115, and id:z0112 precedes it. The **Measure first** bullet is id:z0123, done first; this task decides from its answers.
    - **Order (review, 2026-11-11):** also after id:z0184. If the stdlib's share of each compile (about 85% of 14 ms) can be cut for every run, the saving left for a result cache shrinks, and this task weighs it against the record of the mechanisms that skip work (the stamp, the tiers, id:z0114's R4).
    - **Weighed (reviewing session, 2026-11-14):** id:z0123 showed that the same inputs give the same verdicts. That rules out a test that flips by itself as a source of wrong hits, but not the two that matter: a key that misses an input (how the stamp failed) and a wrong verdict stored under a right key (id:z0114's R4). The design's safeguard against both is a 10% random sample. That catches a single stale entry in a given review about one time in ten, and a missed input outside the change only when the sample lands on it. So a review that took verdicts from the cache would rest on complete input lists for every item kind, gates included, and on that sample: a weaker basis than today's fresh reviewer run. The saving is also smaller than when this task was written. `make test` is about 2 minutes (`Total: ... (119.9s)` at git:7cf8c3e), not 4. The reviewer's reruns in this week's check-ins (id:83cp1, id:ed5ta) were the targeted checks and the fresh differential (248 s), not the whole suite. And the differential has its own base-side cache for the author's runs (id:z0114).
    - **Decided (the maintainer, 2026-11-14): no result cache.** Neither a cache that reviews may cite, nor one that serves only the author's runs. Review runs stay fresh, and the time goes into making the runs themselves cheaper, which pays on every run and has nothing to go stale. id:z0112's review rule is unchanged. To reopen it: id:z0123's measurements stand, and a new design would have to show, with planted stale entries and a planted missed input, that they are caught on every review, not by sampling.

- [x] +testinfra +diagnosis +AI-D @testinfra Z3b Why the ZIR verifier spends about 2 ms on a `continue` from a match arm inside a loop id:mrzb3
    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** found by id:z0184
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Depends:** id:0f0vv, id:at0d6
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-13 git:ff6e64b

    - **Why:** id:z0184's scratch timers (its **Measured** bullets) put the cost in `ZirVerifier.verify` (`src/driver/module.zrl`, `run_body_passes_in_scratch`): `fn with_continue` 2.2 ms, `fn without_continue` 0.18 ms, the same loop written two ways (`build/z184/bis3.zrl`, also in id:z0184's text). A `continue` in a plain `if` costs nothing measurable. id:87kcw removes the shape from `io.zrl`, but any user program with it pays the same, and `stdlib/bufio.zrl` (lines 124, 178, 319, 396) and `stdlib/file.zrl` (174) have `continue`s still to classify.
    - **Do:** find which check inside `ZirVerifier.verify` takes the time on this CFG shape (timers around each of its passes, as id:z0184's patch does for the driver's), and why: an iteration count, a per-block copy, a revisit per back edge. Record the cause, a reproducer and the figure here. A fix is a new task. A fix that would change which programs are accepted is out of scope here and goes to the maintainer.
    - **Checks:**
      - C1: the per-pass split of `verify` for `with_continue` and `without_continue`, with the patch recorded here.
      - C2: the cause, shown by a measurement (for example, an iteration count that grows with the shape), not by reading the code.
      - C3: the five `continue` sites in `bufio.zrl` and `file.zrl`, each with its verifier time.
      - C4: no file under `src/`, `stdlib/` or `scripts/` is changed (`git status --short` empty).
    - **Cause (reviewing session, 2026-11-13, `testinfra` at git:ff6e64b, each run pinned with `taskset -c 5`):** the fixed-point loop in `ZirVerifier.verify_function` (`src/check_zir.zrl`, `while changed && iter < 100`) never converges on this shape and stops at its cap of 100 passes. `with_continue` runs 100 passes, `without_continue` 7. What keeps changing is only the **order** of the state's `enum_aliases` list. Ownership, `maybe_live`, borrows and marks are equal from about pass 8 on, and the alias list holds the same entries in a different order on each pass. At pass 96 of `with_continue`, block 1's entry is `[l17<-15, l27<-15]` against `[l27<-15, l17<-15]` the pass before; block 5 is `[l27, l17, l17]` against `[l17, l27, l17]`. Two mechanisms make this. (1) `states_equal` compares `enum_aliases` by position. (2) The list's order is an accident: the merge (`merge_states`, "EnumPayload aliases merge: Union") keeps the first predecessor's order and appends the rest, and the `Let ... EnumPayload` site (`run_stmt`) pushes a new entry even when one for that local is already there, so a loop body re-appends an alias carried round the back edge. The `continue` gives the loop header a second back edge, the two edges carry the list in opposite orders, and the order flips on every pass. The final reporting pass then runs from states that are equal as sets, so no verdict is wrong today: the cost is the 93 extra passes.
      - C1 (per-pass split, scratch patch `build/mrzb3/split.patch`: timers from `time::monotonic_ns` at the start of `verify_function`, after `compute_liveness`, before the reporting pass and at the end, printed as one `MRZB3T <fn> setup= fixpoint= report= us=` line). Three runs on `build/mrzb3/bis3.zrl` (a copy of `build/z184/bis3.zrl`): `MRZB3T with_continue setup=9 fixpoint=2306 report=19 us=2337` (the other two runs: 2367 and 2342 µs in all), and `MRZB3T without_continue setup=8 fixpoint=150 report=19 us=179` (178 and 179 µs). The fixed-point loop is 99% of the time.
      - C2 (measured, not read): the iteration count, from a scratch line after the loop (`MRZB3 <fn> blocks=<n> iters=<iter>`): `MRZB3 with_continue blocks=17 iters=100`, `MRZB3 without_continue blocks=17 iters=7`. With a second scratch compiler whose `states_equal` compares `enum_aliases` as a set (each entry has an entry with the same `local_id` and an equal `source` in the other list), the same function takes `iters=7` and 195 to 211 µs (`build/mrzb3/set.patch`; the positional build is `build/mrzb3/pos.patch`). The changed-state dump (`mrzb3_note` in `build/mrzb3/trace.patch`) printed `own=eq ml=eq` for every block that changed at pass 99, in every function that reached the cap, so only the alias order differed. Over the compiler's own source, 3 of 1,968 verified functions reach the cap with the positional comparison (`Resolver::check_declared_types` 113 blocks, `ZirLowerer::place_through_raw_pointer` 37, `read_to_end_sized_raw<File>` 23), and none with the set comparison.
      - C3 (the five `continue` sites, verifier time per instance, positional against set comparison, three runs each, from `tests/stdlib/test_stdlib_bufio.zrl` and `tests/stdlib/test_stdlib_read_write.zrl` with the `File` instance): `bufio.zrl:124`, `BufWriter::flush`, **reaches the cap**: 100 passes over 26 blocks, 8,202 to 8,272 µs, against 7 passes and 655 to 658 µs. `bufio.zrl:178`, `BufWriter::write`: 6 passes, 557 µs (571 with the set comparison). `bufio.zrl:319`, `BufReader::fill_buf`: 6 passes, 257 µs. `bufio.zrl:396`, `BufReader::read`: 5 passes, 373 µs. `file.zrl:174`, `read_to_end_sized_raw`, **reaches the cap**: 100 passes over 23 blocks, 3,813 to 3,876 µs, against 7 passes and 305 to 309 µs. `flush` is instantiated 9 times in the bufio test and `read_to_end_sized_raw` 3 times in each of the two tests. The unpatched `build/zoril`, 20 compiles each with `--emit-zil -o /dev/null`, takes 147 ms per compile of `test_stdlib_bufio.zrl`, 49 ms of `test_stdlib_read_write.zrl` and 8 ms of `bis3.zrl`.
      - Order and verdicts: does any local have two aliases with **different** sources, so that the order would change what the first-match lookup (`enum_payload_source_borrowed`) finds? A scratch compiler (`build/mrzb3/zoril_dup`) printed one line for each push of an alias whose local already had one. `sh build/mrzb3/dupscan.sh` compiled every non-`_lib` `*.zrl` under `tests/`, `corpus/` and `bench/safety_matrix/probes/` with it. Output `build/mrzb3/dupscan.out`: `same 16403 in 375 files`, with no `DIFFERENT` line. `src/main.zrl`: 3,987 `same`, none different. So in the tree, an order-insensitive comparison sees the same alias facts as the positional one.

    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** the cause found by id:mrzb3, settled by the reviewing session for an `+AI-G` session
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`

    - **Why:** id:mrzb3 found that `states_equal` (`src/check_zir.zrl`) compares the state's `enum_aliases` list by position. So a loop whose back edges carry the same aliases in different orders (a `continue` in a match arm) never compares equal, and `verify_function`'s fixed-point loop runs to its cap of 100 passes. Measured: `BufWriter::flush` takes 8.2 ms to verify per instance against 0.66 ms, `read_to_end_sized_raw` 3.8 ms against 0.31 ms, and 3 functions of the compiler's own source reach the cap. Every duplicate alias in the tree repeats its local's source (id:mrzb3, "Order and verdicts"), so no verdict is expected to change.

It returns true when every entry of `a` has an entry of `b` with the same `local_id` and a `source` that `places_equal` accepts, and every entry of `b` has one in `a`. There is no length check, since a list may hold one alias twice (the `Let ... EnumPayload` site pushes a repeat). If a borrow rule refuses a reference to the field, pass the two states instead and read `a.enum_aliases` and `b.enum_aliases`.

- [x] +testinfra +safety +decision +AI-D Should the ZIR verifier's fixed-point loop fail, rather than report silently, when it reaches its pass cap id:wptpf
    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** found by id:mrzb3
    > **Asked of:** the maintainer. It changes what the checker does on a program it cannot finish analysing.
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-13

    - **Why:** `verify_function` (`src/check_zir.zrl`) stops its fixed-point loop after 100 passes whether or not it has converged, and then runs the reporting pass from the states it has. id:mrzb3 found 3 functions in the compiler's own source and the stdlib's `BufWriter::flush` and `read_to_end_sized_raw` reaching the cap. In every one, the states differed only in the order of a list (id:5a7eh fixes that), so no verdict was wrong. But a loop that really did not converge would be checked from states that are not a fixed point, and a borrow or move fact reached only on a later pass would go unchecked, silently.
    - **Recommendation (the reviewing session's):** after id:5a7eh, nothing in the tree reaches the cap. Make reaching it an internal compiler error naming the function, so a non-converging case is seen rather than checked from a partial state. Measure first that no program in `tests/`, `corpus/`, the safety probes or the store grid reaches the cap (id:5a7eh's C2 scratch lines). The alternative is a warning, or leaving it as it is.
    - **Decide:** an error, a warning, or no change; and whether the cap of 100 stays.
    - **Decided (the maintainer, 2026-11-13):** an internal compiler error. Reaching the cap stops the compile with an ICE that names the function, rather than reporting from a state that may not be a fixed point. The cap stays at 100 (in id:mrzb3's census of `src/`, the most passes any function took without reaching the cap was 29; after id:5a7eh no function in `src/` reaches the cap). Moved from `future.tm.md` to `## Now` on the maintainer's decision; the implementation is the task after this one, with its check-in after it.

    - **Why:** after id:z0157 to id:z0159 the differential still compiles 138,260 programs a run at about 13.6 ms of CPU each (id:z0114's table). Measured 2026-11-11 at git:acc583d, 200 runs each of `timeout 30 build/zoril -I stdlib=stdlib --emit-zil -o /dev/null <file>`, on a quiet host: `fn main() -> i32 { return 0; }` takes 2.17 ms a run, `bench/safety_matrix/probes/117_closure_stored_in_caller_vec.zrl` (which imports `vec.zrl`) takes 14.26 ms, and `timeout 30 /bin/true` alone takes 1.47 ms. So about 12 ms of each importing program, roughly 85%, is spent on the imported stdlib modules, on both sides of every differential and in every per-file test. Cutting that is paid back on every run and has no stale state, unlike a cache (id:z0114's R4).
    - **Do:** (1) split the 12 ms by phase (reading and parsing, type checking, lowering, the checkers, emitting) for `vec.zrl` and for `mem.zrl` importers, using the compiler's own timing output if it has one, or a scratch build with timers recorded here as a patch.     - **Why:** once `wait`, `wait_any` or `try_wait_any` has reaped a child, its `status` is set and its pid may be reused (the `status` field's comment in `stdlib/proc.zrl` says so). `unix_kill` and `kill_group` do not look at `status`, so a call after the reap signals whatever process now has the pid, or for `kill_group` whatever group now has that id. A pgid stays reserved only while a member of the group is alive.
    - **Do:** in `stdlib/proc.zrl`, `Child.unix_kill` and `Child.kill_group` each start with `if self.status.is_some() { return Result.Err(Error.from_linux_errno(3)); }` (ESRCH, the error `kill` gives for a process that is gone). In `kill_group` it goes before the existing `own_group`/pid check. Each doc comment gains one sentence: after the child is reaped this fails with ESRCH and signals nothing, so a group is signalled before `wait` to end what the child left running. `Child.kill` calls `unix_kill` and needs no change. **Settled, so no judgement is left:** refusing is the only safe answer, because a reaped pid cannot be told apart from a reused one. No caller in the tree signals after a reap (C5). id:z0138's pool signals running groups only: on an item's timeout, on fail-fast and on SIGINT/SIGTERM. **Out of scope:** `reap_any` reaping a child that is not in the slice it was given (`wait4(-1)` returns it, and the function then returns ECHILD without recording it anywhere); not changed here.

    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** decided by id:qqp5s, settled by the reviewer for an `+AI-G` session
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Depends:** id:0f0vv
    > **Placed:** first task of the batch after check-in id:0f0vv, the fix id:qqp5s asks for
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-13 git:3ad3176

    - **Why:** id:qqp5s. `tr_expectations` (`scripts/lib/test_runner.sh`) matches each directive anywhere in the file and ignores what it does not recognise. So `// expected exit banana`, `// expected exit 1O` or `//EXPECT: x` leave the test at the default (run, expect exit 0), and it can pass for the wrong reason. A `// expected compile fail` in a later comment would also change the test's kind.
    - **Do (`scripts/lib/test_runner.sh`, POSIX `sh` and POSIX awk; still one awk pass per file):**
      1. Directives are read from the header only: the lines from the top of the file to the first line that is neither blank nor a `//` comment. id:qqp5s checked the 1,122 per-file tests of `tests/` and `corpus/`: no directive appears after the header, so no test changes kind.
      2. In the header, a line is a directive when, after `//` and any blanks, it starts with `expected `, `EXPECT`, `flags`, `link` or `@skip`. It must then be exactly one of these forms, with nothing after it but blanks where no TEXT follows: `// expected exit N` or `// expected exit code: N`, where N is a decimal from 0 to 255; `// expected compile fail` or `// expected compile success`; `// EXPECT: TEXT`, `// flags: TEXT` or `// link: TEXT`; `// @skip: TEXT` (leading blanks allowed, as today). Anything else is malformed. So is a header with two `expected exit` lines, two `flags:` lines, both `compile fail` and `compile success`, or either of those together with `expected exit`. Prose such as `// expects ...` or `// expecting ...` is not a directive; the two such lines in the tree are `tests/error_reporting/warn_redundant_cast.zrl:6` and `tests/language/other/array_to_slice_coerce.zrl:2`.
      3. A malformed header sets `T_KIND=malformed`, with the first offending line's number and text as written (for a conflict, the second line of the pair). `tr_run_file` then prints `[FAIL] FILE (malformed header, line N: TEXT)`, counts one run and one failure, and compiles nothing. `@skip` does not hide a malformed header.
      4. `tests/runner/fixtures/tests/bad_header.zrl` now fails. `scripts/test_runner_output.sh`'s expected totals follow: 17 run, 7 passed, 10 failed, 2 skipped, and 16 run, 7 passed, 9 failed in the `opts_hidden` mode. This changes a test's expected result on purpose, as id:qqp5s decided.
      5. A new scenario, `scripts/test_test_headers.sh` (a `scenario` row of `scripts/test_plan.tsv`, group `integration`), writes its cases under `build/test-headers/` and runs `./scripts/test.sh --verbose` on them with `TR_WORK=build/test-headers/work`. Each of these malformed cases must give its `[FAIL] ... - [x] +testinfra +tests +AI-G @testinfra Z2b4 `ztest` ends the whole process group of an item that timed out, before it reaps the item id:trx5h
    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** found at check-in id:0f0vv (finding 3), settled by the reviewer for an `+AI-G` session
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Depends:** id:0f0vv
    > **Placed:** after id:bekxx, in the batch that fixes what check-in id:0f0vv found
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-13 git:9969904

    - **Why:** an item that runs past `TR_ITEM_TIMEOUT` gets `kill_group(15)`, then up to 5 s of `try_wait_any`, and `kill_group(9)` only if the item's shell has not been reaped by then. When the shell dies from SIGTERM but something in its group ignores SIGTERM, the shell is reaped in that window and `run_one` returns. Since id:q8rsf, `kill_group` also refuses after a reap, so the group can no longer be reached. The review's probe:
      - The gate `#!/bin/sh` / `( trap "" TERM; exec sleep 611 ) &` / `wait`, run with `TR_ITEM_TIMEOUT=3 build/ztest --gate fixture-scratch-term`, printed `[FAIL] fixture-scratch-term (no result within 3s; its process group was ended)`.
      - Afterwards `ps -eo pid,pgid,comm,args | awk '$3=="sleep" && $5==611'` still listed the `sleep 611`, in the item's group.
      - The header comment's claim was false for that item. id:z0138's pool (fail-fast, SIGINT, SIGTERM) needs the same order.
    - **Do:**
      1. `stdlib/proc.zrl`: `pub fn has_exited(self: &mut Child) -> Result<bool, Error>`. It returns true once the child has ended, without reaping it. With `status` already set, it returns `Ok(true)` with no syscall. Otherwise it calls `waitid(P_PID, pid, &info, WEXITED | WNOHANG | WNOWAIT)`: syscall 247; `P_PID` 1, `WEXITED` 4, `WNOHANG` 1, `WNOWAIT` 0x01000000. `info` is a 128-byte `siginfo_t`, zeroed first; the child has ended when `si_pid`, the `i32` at byte offset 16, is not 0. EINTR (-4) is retried, as in `reap_any`, and any other error is returned. Its doc comment says why it exists: a child that has ended but is not reaped keeps its pid and its group id, so `kill_group` between `has_exited` and `wait` still reaches what it left in its group. A `// SAFETY:` line goes on the syscall, as on the others in the file.
      2. `tools/ztest/src/main.zrl`, `run_one`: poll with `has_exited` every 20 ms instead of `try_wait_any`, and on a normal end reap with `wait()` (what an item leaves running after a normal end is not changed here). On the timeout: `kill_group(15)`, then poll `has_exited` for up to 5 s, then `kill_group(9)` whether the child has ended or not (it is not reaped, so its group id is still its own), then `wait()`. An error from `has_exited` or `wait` sends `kill_group(9)`, reaps with `wait()`, and counts the item as "the worker left no result". The `Vec<Child>` of one goes.
    - **Checks:**
      - C1: a new test, `tests/stdlib/test_proc_has_exited.zrl`, using a grouped `sleep 30`:
        - `has_exited` is `Ok(false)` while it runs.
        - After `kill_group(9)`, it becomes `Ok(true)` within 1 s, and the pid's `/proc/<pid>/stat` state is `Z` (not reaped).
        - `wait()` then returns signal 9, and `has_exited` is `Ok(true)` after it.
        - Quote `./scripts/test.sh --verbose tests/stdlib/test_proc_has_exited.zrl` (`exit code: 0`).
      - C2: the review's probe, with the scratch gate above (never committed). `TR_WORK=build/trx5h/w TR_ITEM_TIMEOUT=3 timeout 60 build/ztest --gate fixture-scratch-term` prints the `[FAIL]` line. Then `ps -eo comm,args | awk '$1=="sleep" && $2==611' | wc -l` prints `0`; before the change it prints `1`. Do not clean up with `pkill -f 'sleep 611'`: it matches the shell running the command and kills it. Kill by pid from `ps` instead, then delete the gate.
      - C3: take-out. Put back "`kill_group(9)` only if not yet ended" (a scratch edit), watch C2 print `1`, quote it, restore.
      - C4: id:655rf C7's case (`sleep 600 & wait`) still ends with nothing left; quote the count.
      - C5: `grep -c proc.zrl build/closure.txt` prints `0` (the `--emit-deps` line in `AGENTS.md`).
      - C6: `make man-gen` and `sh scripts/test_man_pages.sh`; the recorded figures `scripts/check_safety_figures.sh` asks for, in the same commit. Then `make test` and `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`, each `Total:` line quoted. The completion note says the fuzz record is stale.
    - **Completion (generalist, 2026-11-13, git:9969904):** `Child.has_exited` added to `stdlib/proc.zrl`; `ztest`'s `run_one` polls it, and on a timeout sends `kill_group(15)`, polls up to 5 s, sends `kill_group(9)` unconditionally, then `wait()`; the `Vec<Child>` is gone.
      - C1: `./scripts/test.sh --verbose tests/stdlib/test_proc_has_exited.zrl`: `[PASS] ... exit code: 0`.
      - C2: the task's `ps` command cannot match (`-eo comm,args` puts `611` in `$3`, not `$2`), so the count used `ps -eo pid,comm,args | awk '$2=="sleep" && $4==611'`. With the scratch gate: `[FAIL] fixture-scratch-term (no result within 3s; its process group was ended)` and count `0` (start count was 0). Scratch gates deleted. - [x] +testinfra +stdlib +AI-G @testinfra Z1g `wait_any` and `try_wait_any` reap only the children they are given id:ppvzh
    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** found at check-in id:0f0vv (finding 2), settled by the reviewer for an `+AI-G` session; id:q8rsf left it out of scope
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Depends:** id:0f0vv
    > **Placed:** after id:trx5h, in the batch that fixes what check-in id:0f0vv found
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-13 git:3d9e208

    - **Why:** `reap_any` (`stdlib/proc.zrl`), behind `wait_any` and `try_wait_any`, calls `wait4(-1)`, which reaps any child of the process. If the child it reaps is not in the slice, the call returns ECHILD and the status is lost. That child's own `Child` handle then never learns it was reaped, so its `status` stays unset and id:q8rsf's guard cannot stop a later `kill` from signalling a pid that may be reused. Also, `tools/ztest`'s `run_one` reads an error from `try_wait_any` as "the item ended". The pool of id:z0138 holds its items in one slice, but `ztest` also starts the planner and the stray-files scripts with `wait()`, and a library user may mix the two.
    - **Do (`stdlib/proc.zrl`):**
      1. `try_wait_any`: for each child of the slice with no `status`, `wait4(pid, &st, WNOHANG)`. A result above 0 records the status and returns that index. 0 moves on to the next child. An error is returned. If none has ended, return `Ok(None)`. With no unreaped child, return ECHILD as today.
      2. `wait_any`: loop. `waitid(P_ALL, 0, &info, WEXITED | WNOWAIT)` (syscall 247; `P_ALL` 0, `WEXITED` 4, `WNOWAIT` 0x01000000) blocks until some child can be waited for, and reaps nothing. Then run step 1's pass over the slice, and return the index if it found one. If not, the waiting child is not in the slice: return `Err(ECHILD)` without reaping it. EINTR is retried.
      3. The doc comments of both say that a child the call was not given is left for its own handle to wait for. `doc/spec/standard_library.md` §4.4 says the same in its `wait_any` line.
    - **Checks:**
      - C1: a new test, `tests/stdlib/test_proc_wait_any_own.zrl`, with two children: A, `sleep 1`, in the slice, and B, `/bin/true`, not in it. Wait until `/proc/<B>/stat` shows `Z`.
        - `try_wait_any([A])` returns `Ok(None)` while A runs, and B's handle `wait()` then returns exit 0: B was not taken.
        - With a fresh B, `wait_any([A])` returns ECHILD at once. B's `wait()` then returns its status, and a second `wait_any([A])` returns A's index once A ends.
        - Quote `./scripts/test.sh --verbose tests/stdlib/test_proc_wait_any_own.zrl`.
      - C2: take-out. Put `wait4(-1)` back in a scratch edit and watch C1 fail; quote the `[FAIL]` line, then restore.
      - C3: `tests/stdlib/test_stdlib_proc_wait_any.zrl`, `test_proc_kill_reaped.zrl` and `test_proc_new_group.zrl` pass. `sh scripts/test_runner_output.sh --both` passes, since `ztest` uses `try_wait_any`.
      - C4: `grep -c proc.zrl build/closure.txt` prints `0`.
      - C5: `make man-gen` and `sh scripts/test_man_pages.sh`; the recorded figures in the same commit. Then `make test` and `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`, each `Total:` line quoted. The completion note says the fuzz record is stale.
    - **Completion (generalist, 2026-11-13, git:3d9e208):** `reap_any` is replaced by `reap_listed` (wait4 by pid with WNOHANG over the unreaped children of the slice). `try_wait_any` is `reap_listed`; `wait_any` runs it, then blocks on `waitid(P_ALL, 0, ..., WEXITED | WNOWAIT)`, runs it again, and returns ECHILD if only a child outside the slice ended. No loop is needed: the second pass catches any slice child that ended. Doc comments and `doc/spec/standard_library.md` §4.4 say that other children are left to their own handles.
      - C1: `./scripts/test.sh --verbose tests/stdlib/test_proc_wait_any_own.zrl`: `[PASS] tests/stdlib/test_proc_wait_any_own.zrl (1135ms)`, `exit code: 0`.
      - C2: take-out (`wait4(-1)` in `reap_listed`): `[FAIL] tests/stdlib/test_proc_wait_any_own.zrl (wrong exit code)`, `exit code: 2`; restored.
      - C3: `test_stdlib_proc_wait_any`, `test_proc_kill_reaped`, `test_proc_new_group` each `Total: 2 run, 2 passed, 0 failed`; `sh scripts/test_runner_output.sh --both` last line `[PASS] opts_hidden output follows the grammar and its counts agree (build/ztest)` (after `make ztest`).
      - C4: `grep -c proc.zrl build/closure.txt` prints `0`.
      - C5: `make man-gen` wrote `doc/man/zoril-proc.3`; `[PASS] man-pages: all pages build cleanly and match tools and stdlib`. Figures: `doc/SAFETY.md` §5.3 stdlib lines 6,733 and unsafe blocks 188; `unsafe_policy.md` 188 blocks, 532 of 4,849 lines, 10.97%; `check_safety_figures.sh --all` shows no FAIL. After the last edit: `make test`: `Total: 3274 run, 3274 passed, 0 failed, 94 skipped (119.2s)`; `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`: rc 0, `reject-diff: base verdicts: fresh (no cache); base front end 111 s`, `0 newly accepted ... 0 newly refused, of 69145 programs`, `Total: 1195 run, 1195 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (44.9s)`. The fuzz record is stale (`stdlib/` changed). Host-specific `bench/` files were deleted.
      - One behaviour to review: an already-ended unreaped child outside the slice makes `wait_any` return ECHILD at once even while a slice child still runs (the task's rule); a caller mixing handles must `wait()` such children first.

    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** found by id:z0137 (its **Found** item 3), settled by the reviewer at check-in id:0f0vv for an `+AI-G` session; the default decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-13

    > **Depends:** id:0f0vv
    > **Placed:** after id:ppvzh, in the batch that fixes what check-in id:0f0vv found
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-13 git:6a00117

    - **Why:** a `Command` with no `env_*` call starts its child with an empty environment, as id:z0132 made it (`env_set`'s doc comment says so). So `ztest` asks for the parent's environment by removing a name nobody sets (`inherit_env`, `env_remove("ZTEST_UNSET_NAME")`, in `tools/ztest/src/main.zrl`). That works, but it reads as a trick, and the next user of `Command` will meet the empty environment the way id:655rf did: as a bug that no comparison showed.
    - **Decided (the maintainer, 2026-11-13):** a `Command` with no `env_*` call and no `set_envp` inherits the parent's environment, as most process libraries do. `env_clear()` gives an empty one. No `env_inherit` method is added: inheriting is the default. This replaces the reviewer's first plan for this task (an explicit `env_inherit`, the default left alone).
    - **What depends on the empty default today.** Every `Command.new_raw` in `tools/zbuild/src/` except the hosted link: the compiler and zilc (`graph.zrl:165`, `build.zrl:121`, `build.zrl:135`), qbe (`tools.zrl:150`, `build.zrl:141`), the assembler (`build.zrl:148`) and the static link (`build.zrl:394`, when not hosted; the hosted branch already calls `env_clear` and sets `PATH`). Each of them builds a release artifact, and the reproducibility claim (`doc/reproducible_builds.md`) relies on none of them seeing the caller's environment. Each gets an explicit `env_clear()`, so what they see does not change. The tests' spawns (`tests/stdlib/`, `tests/unit/test_empty_compile_and_tool_errors.zrl`) and `ztest`'s are fine with inheriting.
    - **Do:**
      1. `stdlib/proc.zrl`, `spawn`: build the environment with `build_envp` when `env_touched` is set or when `set_envp` was not used (`self.envp` is null). With neither, `build_envp` starts from `/proc/self/environ` as it does for an `env_*` call. Drop the empty-environment fallback (the `@alloca` of one NULL slot) if nothing reaches it any more. The doc comments on the struct's env fields, `env_set` and `env_clear` say the new default. A spawn now reads `/proc/self/environ`, and so fails where it cannot be read; the doc comment on `spawn` says so, as `env_set`'s already does for the `env_*` path.
      2. `tools/zbuild/src/`: `env_clear()` after each `Command.new_raw` listed above, with one comment at the first saying why (the build must not depend on the caller's environment). The hosted link's comment ("A child starts with an empty environment") is reworded.
      3. `tools/ztest/src/main.zrl`: remove `inherit_env` and its two calls, and the comment above it.
      4. `doc/spec/standard_library.md` §4.4: the `env_*` line says a command inherits the parent's environment unless `env_clear` runs or `set_envp` is used.
      5. `tests/stdlib/test_proc_cwd_env.zrl`: a seventh case, a command with no `env_*` call on `/usr/bin/env`, whose output holds the parent's first `/proc/self/environ` entry.

    > **Created:** 2026-11-11
    > **Branch:** `vecclone`
    > **After:** id:z0171.
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-11 git:6a8650d

    - **Direction (decided by the maintainer, 2026-11-11):** as Rust: `resize(new_len, value: T)` and `extend_from_slice(slice)` with `T: Clone`, cloning into every new slot. If stage1 cannot compile it, a re-pin is acceptable (the maintainer's approval, 2026-11-11).
    - **Facts to settle, each by a probe:**
      - Stage1: does `bootstrap/stage1`'s compiler accept a generic method of `Vec<T>` calling `val.clone()` on a `T`? Nothing in the `src/` closure does it today. Build a scratch closure module with `build/zoril-stage1`.
      - Reach: the trait is in `core.zrl` but the integer, `bool` and `Option` impls are in `clone.zrl`, which imports `vec.zrl`; `vec.zrl` cannot import it back. Move the primitive impls to `core.zrl`, or another way.
      - Coverage: which `Copy` types have no `Clone` (references, `fn` pointers, tuples, arrays, a `Copy` user struct without `#[derive(Clone)]`)? Rust's `Copy: Clone` would keep `extend_from_slice` on them accepted; decide whether a structurally `Copy` `T` clones bitwise without an impl, and where (type checker or mono).
      - Enforcement: an impl-level `T: Clone` bound is not checked today (id:z0175); confirm that per-instance resolution of `.clone()` refuses a `T` with no `Clone`.
      - Cost: `String` appends go through `extend_from_slice` on `u8`; measure the cost of a call per byte against `bench/` before choosing a bitwise fast path for `Copy` `T`.
    - **Checks:** each fact above with its probe (program and output) in this task; the decision in one paragraph with the rule it enforces.
    - **Probed (2026-11-11, on `vecclone` at git:fc55a0a's compiler; scratch `build/v2/`):**
      - Stage1: settled, no re-pin. `struct W<T> { x: T } impl<T> W<T> { fn dup(self: &W<T>) -> T { return self.x.clone(); } }` with `impl Clone for u32` in the same file: `build/zoril-stage1 -I stdlib=stdlib --emit-zil` exits 0 with and without `impl<T: Clone>`, and its ZIL calls the impl from the instance (`f17: u32 ...W_Tu32::dup(..)` holds `let _t3 = u32::clone(_t2)`). The same body on a `T` with no `Clone` (`struct N { a: i32 }`) is refused by both (`build/zoril`: `error: no field 'clone' on 'N'`, located in the generic body, not at the call).
      - Coverage: `Copy` is the only bound the compiler satisfies structurally (`src/resolve.zrl:761`, the `Copy` lookups in `src/mono.zrl`, `src/lower_zir/utils.zrl`, `src/driver/types.zrl`); `Clone` needs an impl, and the parser writes one for `#[derive(Clone)]`. So `&T`, `fn` pointers, tuples and arrays have no `Clone` today.
      - Reach: `stdlib/string.zrl` appends bytes with `extend_from_slice` (3 calls), so `Vec<u8>` must find `Clone for u8` from there; that impl is in `clone.zrl`, which imports `vec.zrl` and `string.zrl`. The primitive impls move to `core.zrl`, beside the trait.
      - Users outside `src/`: 12 calls in 10 files, all in `tests/stdlib/test_vec.zrl` (`resize` on integers) and safety probes. Probes 418 (`compile_reject`), 420 (`accept`) and gap_56 call `extend_from_slice` on `Vec<[u8]>`, which `impl<T: Clone> Clone for [T]` (`clone.zrl`, returns `*self` with `#[borrows()]`) covers. A direct `out.push(s.clone())` of a stack view `s` is still refused (`region escape: a pointer to local stack storage is written to memory that outlives this function`, `build/v2/c_slice_clone.zrl`), so the `#[borrows()]` does not launder the borrow there. The risk is the summary route: with a `clone` call between the slice element and the store, `extend_from_slice`'s summary must still tie `slice`'s elements to `self`. id:z0173 must show 418 and gap_56 still refused and 420 still accepted, whole-program and through zbuild.
      - Cost: copying 64 MiB 8 times into a `Vec<u8>`'s buffer (`build/v2/bench_{direct,clone,fill}.zrl`, a generic `copy_into<T: Clone>` writing `src[i]` or `src[i].clone()`, timed with the shell's `time`, two runs each): direct `0.464 s`/`0.462 s`, clone `0.870 s`/`0.870 s`, the fill alone `0.182 s`/`0.183 s`; so 0.55 ns a byte written directly and 1.34 ns through `u8::clone`, about 2.4x on the copy. `src/` builds text with `ByteVec` (`stdlib/bytevec.zrl`, its own `push_slice`), not `String`, so the compiler does not pay it; a user's `String` append would.
    - **Decision (2026-11-11):** the rule is "a `Vec` method never makes a `T` it did not get by value or by `clone`".
      - `extend_from_slice(slice)` writes `slice[i].clone()` into each slot, element by element (the gap_56 rule); `resize(new_len, value)` writes `value.clone()` into each new slot and drops `value`; `ensure_len` becomes `unsafe fn` (it leaves zero bytes, which only a caller that writes them before reading may allow).
      - `Clone` stays an impl, as today: a `Copy` type with no impl (`&T`, a `fn` pointer, a tuple, an array) cannot call the two methods, and `.clone()` resolving per instance refuses it (`no field 'clone' on ..`, a located error in `vec.zrl`, with the call site in the note it gives). Rust's `Copy: Clone` (every `Copy` type cloning bitwise without an impl) is a type-checker change with its own differential, filed separately rather than made a dependency of this fix. So gap_73 and gap_74 (`Vec<&i32>`, `Vec<fn() -> i32>`) become `compile_reject`, not `accept`.
      - The primitive impls (`bool`, every integer, `char`) move from `clone.zrl` to `core.zrl`, beside the trait, so `vec.zrl` reaches them without importing `clone.zrl`; `clone.zrl` keeps the generic and collection impls.
      - `String`'s appends (3 in `string.zrl`) and `bufio.zrl`'s use a `Vec<u8>`-only byte append in `vec.zrl` that keeps today's direct write, so they do not pay the 2.4x; it is sound because a `u8` has no `Drop` and carries no address.
      - Stage1 compiles all of it (probed above); no re-pin.
    - **Completion (2026-11-11):** a decision task: no code changed. Every fact in **Facts to settle** is answered by its probe under **Probed**, on the `vecclone` tree at git:6a8650d (the compiler of git:fc55a0a), and the decision with its rule is under **Decision**. id:z0174 now expects `gap_73` and `gap_74` to become `compile_reject`; Rust's `Copy: Clone` is id:z0179 (`future.tm.md`).

    - **Found (2026-11-10, id:z0167 review, F5):** `defer inner()?;` in `fn outer() -> Result<i32, i64>` causes `build/zoril` to segfault (`exit 139`, stack overflow). `lower_try_expr` calls `self.emit_scope_cleanup(0 as usize, span, ...)`, and `emit_scope_cleanup` (`src/lower_zir/decl.zrl:381-392`) lowers `self.scope_defers[depth]` while `self.scope_defers[depth]` is still populated, so an early return inside a `defer` expression re-lowers the same `defer` infinitely.
    - **Do:** refuse `?` (and any early return) inside a `defer` expression with a located compile error, as `defer` runs during scope exit (`doc/spec/` updated to state the rule).
    - **Checks:**

      - C3: `make test` and `make preflight-changed`, each `Total:` line quoted.
    - **Fixed (2026-11-11, git:fc55a0a on `main`):** `emit_scope_cleanup` raises `defer_depth` and records the scope being exited (`defer_scope_depth`) while it lowers a scope's defers; `lower_try_expr` (`cannot use \`?\` inside \`defer\``), both `return` lowerings (`cannot \`return\` inside \`defer\``) and `lower_loop_jump` for a loop at or outside that scope (`cannot \`break\`/\`continue\` out of \`defer\``) refuse with a located error. A `defer` that reported an error is cleared from its scope (keyed on a new `error_count`, not on `had_error`), so its error is not repeated at every exit. `surface_syntax.md` §7.3 and `standard_library.md` §5.3 state the rule. Begun by an earlier session, which ran out before finishing; its `EXPECT` line did not match the diagnostic and its dedup keyed on `had_error`.

With `timeout -k 5s 60s`: `Segmentation fault`, `exit 139 after 10s`. Restored and rebuilt; the filter above passes again (`Total: 8 run, 8 passed` for `in_defer|defer_`).

And when `inner_same() -> Result<Guard, i64>` is propagated in `fn outer() -> Result<Guard, i64>`, `let v = inner_same()?;` or `let x = inner_same(); let v = x?;` fails with `error: use of moved value`.
    - **Cause:**
      - In `lower_try_expr` (`src/lower_zir/expr.zrl:2971`), `self.emit_scope_cleanup(0 as usize, span, 0 as u32, true)` passes `exclude_id = 0` instead of `early.base` (unlike `lower_return_expr` at line 3136, which passes `ret_place.base`), so `emit_scope_cleanup` emits `ZirStmt.Drop(early)` before `ZirTerminator.Ret(early)`.

When lowering switches to `success_block`, `fresh` stays in `self.scope_locals`, so the normal return's `emit_scope_cleanup` in `success_block` emits `ZirStmt.Drop(fresh)` on a path where `fresh` was never initialized.

- [x] +stdlib +tests +AI-G id:z0130 Z1a `proc.zrl`: wait for whichever child ends first, with or without blocking
    > **Created:** 2026-11-07
    > **Context:** by id:z0117.
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Before:** id:z0137.
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-10 git:3bfec60

    - **Completion note (2026-11-10):** `proc::wait_any(children: [mut Child]) -> Result<usize, Error>` blocks until an unreaped child in the slice ends and returns its index; `proc::try_wait_any` is the `WNOHANG` form and returns none when nothing has ended. Both reap with `wait4(-1)` and keep the status on the `Child` (a private `status: Option<ExitStatus>`); `Child::wait` returns it without calling `wait4`, and a plain `wait` caches its result too. With no unreaped child in the slice, or when `wait4(-1)` reaps a pid that is not in it, the result is ECHILD. Checks, all against `3bfec60`:
      - C1: `scripts/test.sh --filter test_stdlib_proc` prints `[PASS] tests/stdlib/test_stdlib_proc_wait_any.zrl (816ms)` and `Total: 3 run, 3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (0.9s)`; the test starts the 0.2 s and 1 s sleepers in both orders and exits 0 only if the shorter one is returned first each time, with a successful status.
      - C2: the same test polls `try_wait_any` (none first, then index 0 within a 5 s bound).
      - C3: the same test calls `Child::wait` on the reaped child and fails if it takes over 100 ms.
      - C4: the same test, `sh -c 'kill -TERM $$'` is reported as `unix_signal() == 15`; it also covers the no-children-left case (ECHILD, not a hang).
      - C5: with `Child::wait`'s cache read changed to `if false && self.status.is_some()`, the same filter printed `[FAIL] tests/stdlib/test_stdlib_proc_wait_any.zrl (wrong exit code) (304ms)` and `Total: 2 run, 1 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (0.4s)`; restored.
      - C6: `make man-gen` printed `zman: wrote 30 module pages`; `sh scripts/test_man_pages.sh` printed `[PASS] man-pages: all pages build cleanly and match tools and stdlib`. The new functions' man text says which call reaps and that `wait` then returns the kept status.
      - C7: `make test`: `Total: 3216 run, 3216 passed, 0 failed, 88 skipped (122.7s)`. `make preflight-changed`: exit 0, its checked-build run `Total: 1170 run, 1170 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (43.7s)`. A first pair of runs failed only on `safety-figures` (the stdlib line and `unsafe` counts in `doc/SAFETY.md` §5.3 and `doc/spec/unsafe_policy.md` were stale); the figures are updated in the same commit and both runs above are after the last edit.
      - Stale record: `bench/fuzz/README.md` describes `stdlib/` before this change (`scripts/check_fuzz_fresh.sh`).

    - **Do:** a safe function in `proc.zrl` that waits for any child of the calling process (`sys_wait4(-1, ...)`), returning which child ended and its `ExitStatus`, and a non-blocking form (`WNOHANG`) that returns none when no child has ended. EINTR is retried as in `Child::wait`. A `Child` whose pid came back this way is marked reaped, so its own `wait` does not wait4 a pid that may have been reused (decide and state how: a status cached on the `Child`, or an error).
    - **Settled (review, 2026-11-07):** the status is cached on the `Child`, and its `wait` returns it without calling `wait4`, so code that waits on each child keeps working whichever call reaped it.
    - **Checks:**
      - C1: a stdlib test with two children, `sh -c 'sleep 0.2'` and `sh -c 'sleep 1'` started in that order and then in the reverse order: the blocking call returns the shorter one first both times, with exit status 0; quote the test's output.
      - C2: the non-blocking form returns none while both children run, then the pid once one has ended (poll with a bounded loop of short sleeps, failing after 5 s).
      - C3: `Child::wait` on a child the new call reaped returns the cached status and does not block (the test finishes within its timeout).
      - C4: a child killed by a signal (`sh -c 'kill -TERM $$'`) is reported with that signal, as `Child::wait` reports it.
      - C5: take the cache out (a scratch edit that makes `Child::wait` call `wait4` again) and watch C3 fail or hang to its timeout; quote it; restore.
      - C6: `make man-gen` and `sh scripts/test_man_pages.sh` pass, and the new functions' man text says which call reaps and what `wait` returns afterwards.
      - C7: `make test` and `make preflight-changed`, each `Total:` line quoted.

- [x] +bug +tests +AI-G id:z0161 A generic function's name is not taken as its result's enum type in `f.Variant`
    > **Created:** 2026-11-08
    > **Context:** by id:z0157's review (B4).
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-10 git:52d3a99

    - **Why:** `enum E { A, B }`, `fn pick<T>(x: T) -> E { return E.A; }`, then `let e = pick.B;` compiles, as `E.B`: `lower_member_access_expr` (`src/lower_zir/expr.zrl`) calls `resolve_sym_type` on any `SymbolKind.Global` before `try_lower_enum_variant_member`, and for a generic function `resolve_sym_type` gives its return type. It is accepted by the compiler before id:z0157 too. Not unsafe (the value is a valid `E`), but a name that is not a type is read as one.
    - **Do:** in `lower_member_access_expr`, try the enum-variant member only when the symbol names a type (`Decl.Struct`, `Decl.Enum`, `Decl.TypeAlias`, or a `SymbolKind.Type`), so a function's name falls through to the field-access error it gets when it is not generic (`no field 'B' on ...`). Change nothing else.

    > **Completed:** 2026-11-10 git:fa097e0

    - **Why:** in a clone with remotes `hom` and `github` and no `origin`, plain `make preflight-changed` on `testinfra` (no upstream, 30+ commits beyond `main`) fails before running anything: `[FAIL] preflight-changed: no base to check the change against: nothing to compare: the working tree equals HEAD, and HEAD has no commit beyond its upstream or a default branch; set PREFLIGHT_BASE=<commit> to name the base`. `scripts/lib/preflight_base.sh` step 3 looks only at `origin/HEAD`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`. Setting an upstream does not cure it: once `testinfra` is pushed, step 2 finds nothing ahead, and step 3 still has no `origin`.
    - **Decided (this session, at the maintainer's request to fix it):** step 3's candidates are every remote's default branch (`<remote>/HEAD` when symbolic, else `<remote>/main`, `<remote>/master`) and the local `main` and `master`; of their merge bases with HEAD that are not HEAD, the one with the fewest commits up to HEAD is the base. The nearest is the right one: here `hom/main` and `github/main` are at git:70b5361, but `main` was merged into `testinfra` at git:97df9b6 (`git merge-base testinfra main`), and a base of 70b5361 would count `main`'s own commits as this branch's change. Where `origin` exists and is the only remote, the result is unchanged.

      - C4: `sh scripts/test_preflight.sh` passing; `make preflight-changed` (no `PREFLIGHT_BASE`) on `testinfra` runs and names its base; `make test`; each `Total:` line quoted.

- [x] +bug +AI-D id:z0160 `lowering_drop_impl` is still set while a `Drop` body's callees are lowered
    > **Created:** 2026-11-08
    > **Context:** by id:z0157's review (B3).
    > **Branch:** `testinfra`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-10 git:616fc22

    - **Lead, not a reproduced bug:** `Driver.instantiate_impl_methods` sets `self.lowering_drop_impl = true` around `instantiate_method` for `Drop::drop`, and `Driver.lower_fn_instance` does not save and clear it, so a function first lowered from inside a `drop` body sees it set. `is_local_function` (`src/driver/module.zrl`) reads it, but returns early unless the build is `-c`, and stdlib on-demand lowering never happens under `-c`; so the only effect could be the linkage of a private function of the module being compiled, called first from its own `Drop` impl, in a `-c` build. It predates id:z0157 (the review found it there).
    - **Note from id:z0159:** If on-demand drop lowering in `ZirLowerer.has_drop_impl` is ever re-introduced, the same flag leak (`lowering_drop_impl` set around `instantiate_method`) would apply to that entry point as well.
    - **C1 reproduced (2026-11-10, git:5f4b33a):** the leak is real; its effect is a private function exported, not a link failure. Programs in `build/z160/`: `m1.zrl` is the task's module (`pub static mut HITS1`, `struct S`, `impl Drop for S { fn drop(self: &mut S) { helper(); } }`, private `fn helper() { HITS1 = HITS1 + 1; }`, `pub fn make1()` making an `S`); `b1.zrl` is the same with `helper();` also called in `make1` before `S` is made; `c1.zrl` has no `Drop` (control); `d1.zrl`'s `drop` calls `other()` while `make1` calls `helper()` (control). `timeout -k 5s 30s ./build/zoril -I stdlib=stdlib -c --emit-zil -o build/z160/X.zil build/z160/X.zrl`, then `grep -E '^(export |local |extern )?f[0-9]+:'`:
      - m1: `f1: unit build::z160::m1::helper() {` (no `local`); b1: `f1: unit build::z160::b1::helper() {` (no `local`: the `Drop` impl is lowered before `make1`, so its call is the first either way).
      - c1: `local f0: unit build::z160::c1::helper() {`; d1: `local f2: unit build::z160::d1::helper() {`, `f1: unit build::z160::d1::other() {` (no `local`).
      - Linked (`build/zbuild ... -o main_a.bin main_a.zrl`, importing `m1` and `m2`; `main_b` the same with `b1`/`b2`): both build, run `rc=0`, and `nm` shows `T z5build4z1602m16helperE` and `T z5build4z1602m26helperE` (global); the c1 program's helper is `t z5build4z1602c16helperE` (local). No duplicate symbol: the name carries the module path, and a specialization stays local before the flag is read (`is_local_function`).
      - **Placement:** `declare_function` is not called in `lower_fn_instance` itself; the only chain is `lower_fn_instance` → `do_lower_fn` → `lower_fn_in_module` → `declare_function` (`rg -n "do_lower_fn\(|lower_fn_in_module\("`: one caller each).     - **Fixed (git:616fc22):** `lower_fn_in_module` saves and clears `lowering_drop_impl` after `declare_function`, restores it at the end. C1 again: m1 and b1 give `local f1: unit build::z160::m1::helper() {` (and b1's); `S::drop` keeps no `local`; d1's `other` becomes `local f1:` too (same route). Linked: `t z5build4z1602m16helperE`, `T z5build4z1602m11S4dropE` (both modules, both variants), runs `rc=0`. Regression test: `scripts/test_modular_mangling.sh` Test 4 over `tests/modular/drop_callee/` (ZIL `local` on `lib_a::helper`, no `local` on `lib_a::S::drop`, `nm` `t`/`T` for both modules, run 0). Taken out (the `= false` line removed, rebuilt): `[FAIL] scenario: modular-mangling` with `FAIL: lib_a::helper is not local in compile-only ZIL` / `23:f1: unit tests::modular::drop_callee::lib_a::helper() {`; restored: `Total: 2 run, 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`.

## Sprint 2026-S1

- [x] +safety +AI-D id:z0165 Store through a raw pointer without dropping the old value (`Vec::push` uninitialized slot drop)
    > **Created:** 2026-11-09
    > **Context:** found while working on id:z0162.
    > **Branch:** `main`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-10 git:70b5361

    - **The hole:** `Vec::push` writes its new element with `*slot = val` through a raw pointer. The lowering previously emitted a drop of the old value before every assignment to a projected place, so `Vec::push` ran the element type's `drop` on the uninitialized slot before writing the value. From safe code, pushing a type whose `drop` writes through a pointer field (or reads garbage) faulted (rc 139).
    - **Reach:** any `Vec<T>` whose `T` (or a field of `T`, or generic instance) has a `Drop`, without the caller writing `unsafe`.
    - **Fix (git:cf3a710):** `place_through_raw_pointer` in `src/lower_zir/utils.zrl`, checked in `handle_assign_drop_and_move` (`src/lower_zir/decl.zrl`): an assignment whose place is reached through a raw pointer (`*p = v`, `(*p).f = v`, `p[i] = v`) writes without dropping the old value, because raw pointer targets may be uninitialized memory. A store through a reference (`*r = v`) still drops. `Vec::set` overwrites a live element, so it moves the old element out and drops it explicitly. Documented in `doc/spec/surface_syntax.md` §7.2.
    - **Expected result update (git:70b5361):** re-recorded the whole-program ZIL hash of `corpus/zrl/33_vec_and_string.zrl`; only source-line comments moved (282 to 287) because `Vec::set` grew by five lines; emitted code is unchanged.
    - **Checks:**
      - C1: new test `tests/stdlib/test_vec_push_does_not_drop_slot.zrl` (10 pushes past initial capacity, a `set`, and 10 pops; verifies drop counts and dropped IDs). Passes (rc 0).
      - C2: reproducers `pg3`, `pg4`, `pg5` exit 0 (previously rc 139). `pg6` and `sib_field` exit 0.
      - C3: fix taken out (scratch edits): (a) lowering change reverted -> test fails with exit 1; (b) lowering change kept, `Vec::set` explicit drop reverted -> test fails with exit 2. Both halves are required.
      - C4: sibling routes probed: (1) struct/Box holding raw pointer (`*holder.ptr = v`) writes without drop (rc 0); (2) slice element store (`s[0] = v`) drops overwritten element as expected for initialized slice memory (rc 0); (3) generic `G<S>` whose field needs drop: `Vec::push` does not drop uninitialized slot (rc 0); (4) separate compilation and `zbuild`: multi-module `Vec::push` with `Drop` compiles and links cleanly (rc 0).
      - C5: `make test`: `Total: 3207 run, 3207 passed, 0 failed, 88 skipped (213.3s)`.
      - C6: `PREFLIGHT_BASE=6a66434 make preflight-changed`: rc 0; fixpoint identical; all mutations caught; `[PASS] reject-diff: 0 newly accepted, 0 newly refused, of 69128 programs against 6a664342c1a35ac6043b8fe04cdee93091de493a`; checked suite `Total: 1156 run, 1156 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (50.0s)`.

- [x] +safety +tests +AI-D id:z0162 A type is dropped with its own `Drop`, not another module's of the same name
    > **Created:** 2026-11-08
    > **Context:** found while reviewing id:z0157's git:8ff8720.
    > **Before:** id:z0159, which changes the same lookup. Probe `gap_68_drop_glue_by_type_name.zrl` (`known_gap`).
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-10 git:6a66434

    - **The hole:** `import "mem.zrl"; struct Arena { x: i64 } fn main() -> i32 { let local = Arena { x: 1 }; return (local.x - 1) as i32; }` compiles with no `unsafe` and faults (`Segmentation fault`, rc 139): its ZIL's `main` calls `stdlib::mem::Arena::drop` on the user's `Arena`. Without the import it exits 0. Every compiler tried does it: HEAD, git:e5c46f4, the compiler before id:z0157 (`build/z157/zoril.before`) and `--lower-all`.
    - **Reproducers** (written out by the script below; to be moved into tests): `d_lib.zrl` is `pub struct S { p: *mut u8 }`, `impl Drop for S { fn drop(self: &mut S) { unsafe { *self.p = 1 as u8; } } }` and `pub fn unused() -> i32 { return 0; }`. Each of these faults (rc 139): `d_user.zrl` (`import "d_lib.zrl"; struct S { x: i64 }`, a local `S` dropped at scope end); `d_vec.zrl` (the same `S` pushed into a `Vec::<S>`); `d_param.zrl` (a user `Arena` passed by value beside `import "mem.zrl"`); and `d_twolibs.zrl` (a second module `r_lib.zrl` with a plain `pub struct S { x: i64 }` and `pub fn make()` that drops one, both modules imported: `r_lib`'s `S` gets `d_lib`'s `drop`). `struct File { x: i64 }` beside `import "io.zrl"` exits 0, but only because `File::drop` closes fd 3 on the user's value. The reverse, a root `S` with a `Drop` and an imported plain `S` (`d_reverse.zrl`), calls no `drop` in `r_lib::make`: whether a type is hit seems to depend on which `drop` is lowered first, not on which module is the root.
    - **Reproducers, verbatim** (the `build/z157f/r2/` copies go with `make clean`): run from the repository root, after `make`, with `sh repro.sh`. It writes every file into `build/z162/`, builds each program whole-program, runs it, and prints its exit code and the `drop` functions its ZIL defines (which one a value gets is in `main`'s `call` lines: `awk '/ main\(/,/^}/' build/z162/<name>.zil | grep call`, then the callee's `fN:` line). Observed on git:65ab308 (the script run from the task text): `d_user`, `d_vec`, `d_param`, `d_twolibs` and `a5` exit 139; `d_reverse`, `d_file`, `m_method` exit 0 (`m_method` calls `d_lib`'s empty-bodied twin `m_lib::S::drop` on the user's `S`); `m_nomethod` and `m_clone` fail to compile with `no field 'get' on 'S'` and `no field 'clone' on 'S'` (right: the methods are `m_lib`'s); `m_copy` fails with `use of moved value 'a'` (wrong, the safe way: without `import "mem.zrl"` it compiles and exits 0).

    ```sh
    set -u
    w=build/z162; mkdir -p "$w"
    cat > $w/d_lib.zrl <<'E'
    pub struct S { p: *mut u8 }
    impl Drop for S { fn drop(self: &mut S) { unsafe { *self.p = 1 as u8; } } }
    pub fn unused() -> i32 { return 0; }
    E
    cat > $w/r_lib.zrl <<'E'
    pub struct S { x: i64 }
    pub fn make() -> i32 { let s = S { x: 8 }; return (s.x - 8) as i32; }
    E
    cat > $w/m_lib.zrl <<'E'
    import "clone.zrl";
    pub struct S { p: *mut u8, q: i64 }
    impl S { pub fn get(self: &S) -> i64 { return 100; } }
    impl Clone for S { fn clone(self: &S) -> S { return S { p: self.p, q: 200 }; } }
    impl Drop for S { fn drop(self: &mut S) { } }
    pub fn unused() -> i32 { return 0; }
    E
    cat > $w/a5.zrl <<'E'
    import "mem.zrl";
    struct Arena { x: i64 }
    fn main() -> i32 { let local = Arena { x: 1 }; return (local.x - 1) as i32; }
    E
    cat > $w/d_user.zrl <<'E'
    import "d_lib.zrl";
    struct S { x: i64 }
    fn main() -> i32 { let s = S { x: 8 }; return (s.x - 8) as i32; }
    E
    cat > $w/d_vec.zrl <<'E'

    import "vec.zrl";

    E
    cat > $w/d_param.zrl <<'E'

    E
    cat > $w/d_twolibs.zrl <<'E'

    E
    ```
